category: anonymous file host with password and burn-after-reading

free_tier.stated: Upload files up to 10GB each. Password protect, burn after reading, or just share. No account needed.

retention.stated: The uploader chooses how long a file exists, and when the timer runs out the file is permanently deleted; there is no early delete, only the chosen timer. unverified: the selectable timer values and their maximum are not listed on the page.
retention.notes: Burn-after-read is a pull-count of one, not a retention period.

egress.terms: No byte allowance stated; a burn-after-reading option makes the first read the last.

interface_detail: Browser drop zone. /api/upload returned 400 (a validation answer) so a JSON endpoint answers, but no contract is published.
tooling: Browser only as observed; the 400 on /api/upload is the opening for a wrapper.
chaining: Burn-after-read is the right primitive for handing a credential or a one-shot dataset to a reader without leaving a copy; it is the opposite of an archive.
limits_note: Retention is a timer the uploader selects at upload, and early deletion is not offered; the selectable timer values and any rate limit are not published. Whether a datacenter address is accepted: not published.
binding_note: The pull count breaks before the size does.

identity_cost.detail: 'No account needed' on the page and the FAQ says no registration or personal details are required; request IP addresses are logged temporarily to prevent abuse. No upload was attempted.

reliability_note: A single-screen drop zone with an FAQ; no rate limit, maximum timer or datacenter-address policy is published, and request IP addresses are logged temporarily to prevent abuse.
confidence_note: The offer sentence and the FAQ are quoted from the vendor page. Retention is a timer chosen at upload whose selectable values are not published, and the upload path contract is not published; no upload was attempted.
